notes: The DS-ECO-6 corpus line ('nothing organised behind it') is the exact phrasing the brief lists as REFUSED on a town whose rows seat a street gang and front businesses, and this town seats both. The corpus claim and the contradiction table point opposite ways; I kept the 'minor / never grew' half of the claim and dropped the 'nothing organised' half rather than ship a refused line.

Several corpus lines break the brief's own bars: a colon in DS-ECO-1, a semicolon in DS-GEN-18, and 'you will be given' in DS-ECO-12's income spine (a future indicative plus an address to the reader). The brief says not to imitate a breach, so I re-cut all three, but a fallback line that would be dropped by the instruments is an odd thing to be handed as the claim.

The rule 'the second sentence must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is unusable where every listed field is UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD (DS-ECO-1, DS-ECO-10, DS-GEN-18) or is a schema path whose 'own word' has no plain-English form (incomeSources.reduce, economicState). I wrote single sentences there, which may be thinner than intended.
DS-ECO-12's income key says 'two or three sources between them' while the field it reads says incomeSources.length = 10. I wrote to neither number, but the key and the field appear to disagree.

The DS-ECO-6 pool is marked dm-only with the note 'the unit itself is the notebook and still rides in spine', while the per-pool notebook instruction says 'none, return an empty list'. I returned an empty notebook and wrote the spine in the notebook register, but the two lines read as if they could also mean one notebook row.
